families.topic: IMT terms of reference, membership, leadership, decisions, agendas, minutes and governance
evidence_points: The toolkit supports establishment and operation of incident management teams.
An IMT should agree incident aims and objectives at its first meeting.
IMT membership should reflect the population, pathogen, scale, controls, expertise and assessed risk.
The chair provides strategic leadership and facilitates coordinated, shared decision-making.
Minutes should record evidence, differing views, decisions, reasons, actions, owners and timeframes.
The toolkit includes templates for terms of reference, agendas and meeting minutes.

families.topic: structured epidemiological, microbiological, environmental and operational outbreak investigation planning
evidence_points: The toolkit supports development of a structured outbreak investigation protocol.
Investigation planning should define aims, case definitions, data requirements and responsibilities.
Epidemiological investigation should describe cases by person, place and time.
Microbiological evidence can support confirmation, typing and linkage assessment.
Environmental or food-chain investigation may be required when a source or transmission route is suspected.
Protocols should be reviewed as hypotheses, evidence and control priorities change.

families.topic: principles for adapting outbreak management to health, care, education, workplace and communal settings
families.page_title: Toolkit 6: principles for the management of outbreaks in specific settings
evidence_points: The toolkit supports adaptation of outbreak-management principles to specific settings.
Setting characteristics can alter contact patterns, vulnerability and feasibility of controls.
Responsibilities should be agreed between the setting, UKHSA, local authorities, NHS and other relevant partners.
Control measures should be proportionate to the pathogen, population and operational context.
Communication should be tailored to residents, staff, families, visitors and affected communities.
Setting-specific action should remain aligned with disease-specific guidance and local plans.

families.topic: communication strategy, audiences, accessibility, media coordination and misinformation management during outbreaks
evidence_points: The toolkit supports planning and delivery of outbreak communications and media activity.
An incident management team should identify a coordinated communications lead.
Audiences, information needs, language, accessibility and trusted channels should be considered.
Messages should reflect the current risk assessment and agreed control advice.
Internal, partner, public and media communications require coordination and version control.
Communication effectiveness and emerging concerns should be monitored and used to update the approach.

families.source: UKHSA constructive debriefing and lessons identified toolkit
families.topic: no-blame outbreak debriefing, learning capture, action ownership and continuous improvement
families.page_title: Toolkit 8: UHKSA constructive debriefing and lessons identified
evidence_points: The toolkit uses an end-to-end approach to capture learning from incidents and exercises.
Debriefing should capture both good practice and problems, challenges and root causes.
A no-blame culture supports honest participation and organisational learning.
Hot, structured, multi-agency and post-incident debriefs can be used at different times.
Lessons should be assigned, monitored and incorporated into planning and preparedness.
Health inequality impacts and future mitigations should be considered during debriefing.
